name: Drowningman
label: Revelation
lede: A Burlington, Vermont band that went through at least nineteen members in ten years, blew up a tape machine making its best record, and recorded a deliberately terrible album to get off its label.

eras.title: A basement on Hungerford Terrace
eras.text: Burlington had a real heavy-music scene in the mid-'90s, but Drowningman never quite belonged to it. They took cues from Deadguy and Unbroken as much as Sunny Day Real Estate, and spent more time playing Boston and upstate New York than Vermont.

years.p: Simon Brody, Denny Donovan, Javin Leonard, Dave Barnett and Todd Tomlinson start Drowningman. Some of them had played in a Boston emo band before.

q: We didn't really belong to a scene. We still don't.
years.h: Drowningman's first show, in a Hungerford Terrace basement
years.p: Drowningman play for the first time on New Year's Eve in a basement on Hungerford Terrace in Burlington, and start touring almost immediately.
years.xp: Simon Brody told No Echo the band never belonged to a scene and liked working on the periphery. Being in Vermont made that easy: the nearest real circuit was Boston.

years.p: Drowningman sign to Hydra Head, the Boston label that was home to [[Converge|fa31e7d4-a03a-4110-98fc-f8826e95ec25]], and put out their first 7". Guitarist Denny Donovan leaves the same year.

eras.title: Busy signal
eras.text: Hydra Head's Aaron Turner wasn't sure Drowningman could deliver an album after losing a key songwriter. They did it in Vermont, and Steve Evetts' mix changed how they heard themselves.

years.h: Busy Signal at the Suicide Hotline · Hydra Head
years.p: Drowningman's first album, recorded in Vermont and mixed by Steve Evetts. Hydra Head's Aaron Turner had doubted they could pull it off after losing a key songwriter.
years.xp: Simon Brody told No Echo that two hours into Evetts' mix he was astounded by what he was hearing.

years.p: Hydra Head pairs Drowningman with New Jersey's The Dillinger Escape Plan on a split 7". Guitarist Matt Roy joins in 1999.

eras.title: The record that blew up the tape machine
eras.text: Drowningman moved to Revelation and made Rock and Roll Killing Machine through a week of broken gear and cabin fever. The release went badly, the relationship went worse, and the band's answer was a joke album and a breakup.

years.h: How They Light Cigarettes in Prison 7" · Revelation REV 89
years.p: Drowningman's first Revelation release: 220 copies on red vinyl, then 330 on pink.

years.h: Drowningman's Rock and Roll Killing Machine sessions go wrong
years.p: A metal spike through the van floor made Drowningman miss day one. The tape machine's wheel wobbled, the replacement part was wrong, and they waited Monday to Friday without recording.
years.xp:
Simon Brody told Exclaim! they played PlayStation and ate at the same restaurant until they wanted to kill each other. At a second studio, with two songs of drums left, the tape machine started pouring smoke and blew up.

Brody says the adversity made the record what it is.

years.src: Wikipedia · Exclaim! · Revelation Records pressing history
years.h: Rock and Roll Killing Machine · Revelation REV 96
years.p: Simon Brody, Javin Leonard, Matt Roy, Dave Barnett and Joe Villemaire's album gets a 10 out of 10 from Terrorizer. The first vinyl run is 300 red and 1,350 black.

Drowningman step outside Revelation for a 10" and CD on Equal Vision. They tour with [[Converge|fa31e7d4-a03a-4110-98fc-f8826e95ec25]], The Dillinger Escape Plan and [[Glassjaw|429f9fbf-0a0b-4a9e-a88c-94d48aa466ed]] in these years.

years.h: Drowningman record Best Record Ever, badly on purpose
years.p: Fed up with Revelation after a bungled release and an unfunded tour, Drowningman make a deliberately terrible album at [[Kurt Ballou|1e922902-2cb9-499f-aeb5-9a8c51dd0df0]]'s GodCity studio to get out of their deal. Revelation passes, and it's never released.
years.xp:
Ballou produced and threw himself in, playing saxophone and dreaming up absurd tracks. [[Cave In|f3c95ad4-215b-4519-8660-84c9f467da05]]'s [[Stephen Brodsky|a0ff602c-7f3e-472d-8786-953da6cd7591]] covered Ziggy Stardust with new words about Simon Brody, with Converge's [[Ben Koller|b6fdd346-b9e8-449a-9105-612d3722503f]] on drums.

They played it for Revelation's A&R on tour, and the response was dismissive. Louder says the band broke up after the label rejected the work.

years.h: Drowningman's last show, at Krazy Fest 5
years.p: Drowningman break up after playing Krazy Fest 5.

eras.title: Broken up, twice
eras.text: Simon Brody and Denny Donovan revived the name with a new crew and a big-bill tour. It fell apart within a week.

years.h: Learn to Let It Go: The Demos on Law of Inertia
years.p: Drowningman's early demos come out on Law of Inertia as Simon Brody and Denny Donovan put a new line-up together.

years.h: Don't Push Us When We're Hot · Thorp Records
years.p: Drowningman's third album, with Hans Olson, Jamie Durivage and Brian Curry in the band alongside Simon Brody and Denny Donovan.

years.h: Drowningman quit three or four shows into a tour
years.p: On a badly organized tour with The Dillinger Escape Plan, [[Misery Signals|0b0b523f-e9d5-4f18-919c-ebf084a58c26]], [[Every Time I Die|ef90f210-f136-4386-ab37-8c00d04eeace]] and Zao, the disgruntled band breaks up for a second time after three or four shows.
years.xp: Frank Smecker and drummer Dave Joyal had rejoined for the tour. Seven Days counts at least 19 musicians through Drowningman between 1995 and 2005.

eras.title: The Killing Machine line-up, one more time
eras.text: The Rock and Roll Killing Machine line-up played three Northeast shows, including a homecoming in Burlington.

years.h: Drowningman reunite at Signal Kitchen in Burlington
years.p: Simon Brody, Javin Leonard, Matt Roy, Dave Barnett and Joe Villemaire play Signal Kitchen, one of three Northeast reunion shows.

eras.title: Not a nostalgia act, then 'all theater'
eras.text: Drowningman came back with new songs, not just old ones, and Iodine Recordings reissued the debut. Then Simon Brody announced he was leaving, called the statement theater, and put the band on indefinite hiatus.

years.h: Later Day Saints: Drowningman's first new music in 16 years
years.p: Reunited with guitarist Teej Maynard alongside Simon Brody, Javin Leonard and Matt Roy, Drowningman release the Later Day Saints EP on Iodine Recordings.

years.h: Iodine reissues Busy Signal at the Suicide Hotline
years.p: Iodine Recordings puts Drowningman's 1998 debut back on vinyl, remastered by Jack Shirley with two bonus tracks.

years.h: Simon Brody puts Drowningman on indefinite hiatus
years.p: Simon Brody announces an extended, indefinite hiatus to focus on work, family and writing. He had earlier posted an exit statement citing a divorce and living 1,500 miles away, then called it all theater.
